top_stories.title: Sebi imposes penalty on Suzlon, executives for misstating financials - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi)** has overturned an earlier decision that exonerated **Suzlon** and its executives. The regulator will now impose penalties after initiating an investigation in 2019 based on an anonymous complaint alleging irregularities in the company's dealings. Sebi claims that Suzlon improperly valued a business sale, concealed significant liabilities, and misclassified financial obligations, leading to inflated profits and capital raising.

top_stories.title: Worth examining Vijay’s appeal to children to convince adults to vote for him, says judge citing personal anecdote - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Justice G.R. Swaminathan** of the Madras High Court presided over a case involving an appeal by **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to children to vote for his party, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  Senior counsel **S. Muralidhar**, representing TVK, argued that the petition was based on news reports and urged the court to adjourn the matter so he could study it in depth.  **N.R. Elango** and **S.R. Rajagopal**, representing DMK and AIADMK respectively, countered by stating their clients were accused of voter bribery and should be dealt with through election petitions. The case was adjourned until July 1, 2026, for counter affidavits.

top_stories.title: US military strikes another boat in Pacific, bringing death toll above 200 | US military | The Guardian
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **US military** conducted a strike on a suspected drug smuggling boat in the eastern Pacific, killing three men and raising the death toll from recent attacks to 202.  **Gen Francis L Donovan**, commander of US forces in Latin America, authorized the operation, which was announced by **Southern Command** on X (formerly Twitter). The strikes are part of a campaign against alleged drug trafficking vessels operating in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, but critics question their legality due to a lack of evidence.

top_stories.title: Ukraine using AI drones to strike vital Russian supply lines
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Ukraine's** military is using AI-enabled drones, including the Hornet system, to target Russian supply convoys in occupied territories.  The strikes have disrupted logistics and forced Russia to shorten its convoys. **Mykhailo Fedorov**, Ukraine's defense minister, stated that this strategy aims to "increase pressure on the Russian military in the rear." Experts believe these drone attacks are a significant development in the war, as they disrupt crucial supply lines and weaken Russia's ability to sustain offensive operations.

top_stories.title: Gold demand drops 70% after sharp duty hike in India - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **India's** gold import demand fell to about 7.5 tonnes in the fortnight ended May 27, a significant drop from around 25 tonnes a year earlier. The government increased the import duty on gold to 15% from 6%, leading to a 70% decline in demand according to industry estimates. **Joyalukkas**, a gold jewellery retail chain, reported a 35% drop in demand.  **The World Gold Council (WGC)** noted that while large chain stores saw a brief period of panic buying, mid-sized and regional jewellers are continuing to see demand from affluent customers but are expected to rely more on gold exchange programs going forward.

top_stories.title: China building launch pads near nuclear missile silos - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **China** is constructing a vast military complex in the Xinjiang desert, which some security experts believe is designed to protect its nuclear missile silos from potential American first strikes. The complex includes octagon-shaped installations housing personnel and military vehicles, armored bunkers, and airfields. Satellite images show that these structures are connected by extensive networks of roads and conduits, potentially supporting a range of defensive capabilities including mobile air defense missiles and road-mobile ICBM launchers. This network may set China apart from other major nuclear powers, who rely on sheer numbers of silos and hardened construction to deter a first strike.

top_stories.title: Pakistani freelancers outearn regional rivals - Business - DAWN.COM
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Pakistan's** freelancers earned over $950 million in foreign exchange during the first 10 months of fiscal year 2026, a 49% increase from the previous year.  **Dr Imran Batada**, president and CEO of the **Pakistan Freelancers Association (PFA)**, attributed this growth to increased participation on platforms like Upwork and Fiverr, as well as rising awareness among Pakistanis about freelancing opportunities. The PFA is working to organize training sessions for freelancers in emerging trends and payment processes.

top_stories.title: Spain's Sánchez digs in after 8 years as PM, but can he survive wave of scandals?
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Pedro Sánchez**, prime minister of Spain, faces growing pressure as multiple investigations into alleged corruption within his Socialist Party threaten his political survival.  **José Luis Zapatero**, a former prime minister and close ally, is under investigation for alleged influence peddling, while **Leire Díez**, a member of the party, is accused of orchestrating a smear campaign against law enforcement officials. Sánchez's brother, **David Sánchez**, has been put on trial for alleged influence peddling, and his wife, **Begoña Gómez**, faces potential charges related to misuse of funds and influence peddling.  The opposition calls for Sánchez's resignation, while some allies within the coalition government express concerns about the impact of these scandals on upcoming elections. The future of Sánchez's government remains uncertain as investigations continue and political pressure mounts.

top_stories.title: RBI efforts boost rupee usage, yet global adoption remains limited - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has implemented measures to encourage the use of the rupee in cross-border trade. These include allowing correspondent banks in partner countries to open Special Rupee Vostro Accounts with Indian banks and facilitating local currency settlement arrangements with several nations. This initiative aims to support **India's** ambition of becoming a developed economy, as previously stated by former RBI Deputy Governor **T Rabi Sankar**.

top_stories.title: 'They walk among us': White House launches alien-themed website to track immigrants - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **White House** launched a new website, Aliens.gov, focused on immigration enforcement. The site uses imagery and language reminiscent of science fiction to highlight arrests of undocumented immigrants.  It features a live dashboard tracking encounters and arrests across the country, as well as an interactive map displaying arrest data. The platform also includes thousands of pages of immigration records and operational data, aiming to increase transparency about enforcement activity nationwide. Critics argue that the website dehumanizes migrants and encourages public suspicion towards immigrant communities.
